vault.title: CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision Syllabus
vault.summary: This document outlines the 15-week schedule, grading policy, and lab requirements for CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision taught by Abenova Saule. Students will learn core computer vision topics including image filtering, edge detection, feature matching, and convolutional neural networks. The course grade is determined by labs, a midterm exam, and a final project.
key_terms: Convolution: A mathematical operation used in image filtering to apply effects like blurring or sharpening.
Edge detection: Techniques like Sobel and Canny used to identify object boundaries in images.
SIFT: Scale-Invariant Feature Transform, an algorithm to detect and describe local features in images.
Homography: A transformation relating the coordinates of points in one image to another plane.
RANSAC: RANdom SAmple Consensus, an iterative method to estimate mathematical model parameters from noisy data.
CNN: Convolutional Neural Network, a class of deep neural networks commonly applied to analyzing visual imagery.
